APX.AI Secure Transmission — Outlook User Guide (End User)

Audience: First-time users of APX.AI Secure Transmission who do not yet have an APX.AI account.

When you send large or sensitive attachments, APX.AI Secure Transmission moves the file to the APX.AI server and places only a secure download link in the email body, so it never uses up your Outlook attachment quota.

This guide walks you through everything from scratch: install the add-in → confirm the server → request an account → log in → create your private key → send your first secure attachment. We recommend reading it through once before you start.

Prefer to watch first? This guide’s full walkthrough is also available as a video tutorial — click to watch.

1. Install the Add-in

While composing a message in Outlook, open the Insert toolbar, click Get Add-ins, search for “APX.AI”, select APX.AI Secure Transmission, and click Add. After installation, the “APX.AI Secure Transmission” icon appears in the Insert menu — click it to open the add-in.

2. Confirm the Server URL

The first screen after opening the add-in is the server setup. The URL is pre-filled with https://apxlive.ioneit.com, so you can simply click Continue — no manual entry needed.

Only change this field if your organization has given you a dedicated server URL; enter that URL, then click Continue.

3. Request an Account (if you don’t have one yet)

If this is your first time and you don’t have an APX.AI account yet, request one first. On the login screen, click Sign up to open the public sign-up page, fill in the required fields (account, name, email, etc.), and submit. An administrator will review and activate your account.

This is a public sign-up page — never enter your private key password or any sensitive key here. If your organization has already provisioned an account for you, skip this step and log in directly.

4. Log In

Once your account is activated, return to the add-in and log in with your APX.AI account and password.

5. Create Your Private Key

After your first login you land on the private key page. Click Create Private Key, set a private key password (at least 12 characters: 6 letters (3 upper + 3 lower), 3 digits, and 3 special characters), and click Create Private Key.

Once created, it is verified automatically and takes you straight to the upload page — nothing else to do. Remember this private key password: when you switch devices or reinstall the add-in, click Complete Verification, select your private key file, and enter this password.

6. Send a Secure Attachment

  1. On the upload page, choose the file you want to send and click Upload and Generate Link.

  2. Once “Secure Send Complete” appears, the download link is inserted into the email body automatically — just send the email as usual.

7. How to Fill the Recipient Field

The add-in automatically fills the upload page’s “Recipients” field with the part before @ of the first address in Outlook’s “To” field (for example, allen2@ioneit.com fills in allen2). This field is editable — you can type in any APX.AI account directly. The Outlook version detects changes to the “To” field live and keeps the field in sync automatically, but once you edit this field manually, it stops being overwritten unless you click Refresh to re-read it from Outlook’s “To” field.

The recipient must already have an APX.AI account to receive the securely sent file. If they haven’t registered, clicking Upload and Generate Link will show “No APX.AI account found for this recipient. Please confirm they have registered.” — ask them to complete sign-up first (see step 3), then resend.

FAQ

  • How does the recipient download? They click the link in the email and retrieve the file from the APX.AI download page (Chrome recommended).
  • Does the recipient need the add-in installed? No. The recipient only needs to click the link to reach the APX.AI download page; it has nothing to do with whether the add-in is installed.
  • How do I log out? There is a Logout button at the top-right of the upload page.
  • How large does an attachment need to be? Anything over the size threshold triggers a prompt automatically; you can also open the add-in manually at any time.
